chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu 'Ammar al-Sarraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man in whom the thief is found, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is liable (for the debt) if he does not bring the seller with witnesses (to prove the item was stolen from him).'

key_terms.السَّرِقَةُ: The thief or the stolen item

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a person found with a stolen item in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the burden of proof in cases of *gharam* (financial liability) for stolen goods found in one's possession, emphasizing that mere possession does not automatically incur debt. The possessor is exempt from paying the value of the item if they can produce the original seller and witnesses to substantiate the theft claim, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of *al-bayyinah 'ala al-mudda'i* (the proof is upon the claimant). This ruling protects the possessor from arbitrary claims by ensuring the seller's right is verified through credible testimony.
